To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diversity and the clonal spread of penicillin nonsusceptible pneumococcal clones in Iceland is similar to what is seen elsewhere in the world.

the majority of penicillin nonsusceptible pneumococcal strains in Iceland have been introduced from other countries and that the most prevalent clones in Iceland are also found in other parts of the world, indicating that they may have a global distribution.

after the introduction of the multidrug resistant pneumococcal clone Spain(6b)-2, the prevalence of penicillin nonsusceptible pneumococci began to increase, but the majority of clones had genetic backgrounds also observed abroad.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diversity of pneumococci circulating in Iceland after a period of high prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains of Spain(6B) origin.
the genetic diversity and molecular epidemiology of penicillin nonsusceptible S. pneumoniae circulating in the country, with the aim to understand the mechanisms of dissemination of these clones.
the diversity of pneumococci circulating in Iceland after introduction of the multidrug resistant clone Spain(6)-2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the majority of penicillin-intermediate S. pneumoniae isolates detected in Iceland have genetic backgrounds also detected outside the country, singular events of horizontal gene transfer of pbp and capsular genes have been detected.
, although the majority of penicillin-non-susceptible pneumococci circulating in Iceland are genetically related to strains found elsewhere, the majority of strains are not the same.

the majority of penicillin-intermediate pneumococcal clones circulating in Iceland have genetic backgrounds similar to those of clones circulating abroad, and that the majority have probably been imported to the country, followed by local dissemination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pneumococcal population in Iceland is very dynamic and is composed of multiple clones, which may have been introduced into the country repeatedly from abroad.

, after a period of dissemination and clonal spread of the multidrug resistant pneumococcal clone Spain(6b)-2, other clones expressing intermediate resistance to the antibiotic have been introduced and have become the dominant clones in Iceland.
the majority of clones with penicillin resistance circulating in Iceland have a genetic background also detected abroad.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, although the introduction of penA mutations into pneumococcal populations may be a singular event, the dissemination of penA mutations in a population is likely to be a result of the introduction and spread of multiple clones, rather than the horizontal transfer of pbps.
the introduction of penA-mediated intermediate resistance in Iceland was not a single event but rather the result of multiple introductions of penicillin-non-susceptible clones.
the genetic background of pneumococci circulating in a country can be used to determine the origin of the strains.
